chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, that he said:

“The servant does not lead anyone except his own household” is to be understood as pertaining to merit and recommendation, although it is permissible for him to lead his household and others besides his household.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the servant or slave being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.مَحْمُولٌ: interpreted or understood in a particular legal sense
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: to lead in congregational salat (prayer) as Imam

ai.seo_question: Can a servant lead people in congregational salat (prayer), or only his own household?
ai.summary: This report explains that restricting a servant’s leadership in salat (prayer) to his own household is understood as a matter of virtue and recommendation, not strict prohibition. It indicates the permissibility of his leading both his household and others in congregational salat (prayer).
